p.src: Now Fei Bao said to Li Jun, “Though I am but a dull and ignorant fellow, I once heard a wise man say: ‘Every worldly success must end in failure, and every man who rises must someday decline.’ You have pursued your glorious career at Liangshan Marsh for more than ten years now, and moreover have won every one of a hundred battles. When you went to defeat Liao, not a single brother was lost; but in this campaign against Fang La, your edge has plainly been blunted, and Heaven’s allotted span cannot last much longer. Why do you think I have no wish to become an official? It is because the ways of the world are wicked. Once peace is restored, they will surely come, one after another, to take your lives. As the old saying goes: ‘Peace is won by generals, yet generals are not allowed to see the peace.’ How perfectly true those words are! Now that the four of us have sworn brotherhood, why do you three not take advantage of this moment, while your fortunes have not yet run out, and seek a place where you may settle your lives and fulfil your destiny? Gather some money, build a great ship, recruit a few sailors, and find some quiet, suitable haven upon the rivers or seas where we may dwell and live out our natural years. Would that not be splendid?” When Li Jun had heard him out, he fell to the ground in obeisance and said, “My worthy brother, I am deeply indebted to you for teaching me and guiding one so blind and foolish. Your counsel is excellent in every respect. But Fang La has not yet been destroyed, and I cannot cast aside Song Gongming’s kindness and fellowship. I cannot take this step yet. If I followed you worthy brothers away today, I would show no regard at all for the fellowship we have shared throughout our lives. If all of you are willing to wait awhile for me, then after Fang La has been subdued, I shall bring my two brothers and come straight to join you. I earnestly beg you to take us in. You worthy brothers must be sure to prepare this way of escape beforehand. If I betray the words I have spoken today, may Heaven itself reject me! I would be no true man!” The four men said, “We shall ready a ship and wait especially for your arrival, brother. You must never break your promise!” Li Jun and Fei Bao drank together as sworn brothers and settled every detail, vowing never to betray their covenant.

p.src: The next day, Li Jun took leave of Fei Bao and the other three men, then returned with Tong Wei and Tong Meng to report to Commander Song. They said that Fei Bao and his three companions had no wish to become officials and desired only the carefree life of fishermen. Song Jiang sighed over this once more, then gave orders to muster the land and naval forces and set out. With no bandits left in Wujiang County, the army marched straight through Pingwang Town and pressed swiftly onward toward Xiuzhou. Duan Kai, the defending general of that prefecture, learned that Fang Mao, the Third Prince at Suzhou, was dead and thought only of packing up and fleeing. His scouts discovered that the great army was not far from the city. Looking into the distance, he saw banners blotting out the sun along both land and water routes, with ships and horses following one upon another, and was frightened out of his wits. The vanguard generals Guan Sheng and Qin Ming had already reached the foot of the walls, and at once deployed the naval vessels to surround the west gate. From atop the wall Duan Kai called out, “There is no need to attack. We are preparing to surrender.” The gates were opened at once, and Duan Kai, bearing incense, flowers, lamps, and candles, and leading sheep and carrying wine, welcomed Commander Song into the city and escorted him to lodge at the prefectural offices. Duan Kai led the others in paying homage. Song Jiang reassured him, restored him to the status of a loyal subject, and posted proclamations to pacify the people. Duan Kai explained, “We were originally honest people of Muzhou, but Fang La repeatedly harmed and oppressed us, forcing us against our will to submit to his command. Now that Heaven’s army has come here, how could we dare not surrender?” Song Jiang questioned him closely: “Who holds the fortified city of the Ninghai Military Prefecture at Hangzhou? How many troops and able generals are there?” Duan Kai reported, “The walls of Hangzhou encompass a vast area and its population is dense. Dry roads approach it from the east and north, the great river lies to the south, and a lake lies to the west. It is guarded by Fang La’s eldest crown prince, Fang Tianding, Prince of Nan’an. Under him are more than seventy thousand troops, twenty-four battle commanders, and four marshals, making twenty-eight officers in all. The two foremost are particularly formidable. One is a monk from Shezhou known as ‘Precious-Light Tathagata.’ His lay surname is Deng and his religious name is Yuanjue. He wields a monk’s staff forged entirely of solid iron and weighing more than fifty catties, and everyone calls him the Imperial Preceptor. The other is a native of Fuzhou named Shi Bao. He is expert with a meteor hammer and never misses his mark. He also wields a treasured saber called the Wind-Cleaving Saber, which can cut through copper and sever iron; even three layers of armor offer no resistance, for it passes through as though cleaving the wind. The other twenty-six are all handpicked commanders and every one of them is fierce and brave. Commander, you must on no account underestimate the enemy.” After hearing this, Song Jiang rewarded Duan Kai and ordered him to go to Pacification Commissioner Zhang’s headquarters and report all the particulars. Later, Duan Kai accompanied Pacification Commissioner Zhang on campaign and guarded Suzhou, while Deputy Commander-in-Chief Liu Guangshi was assigned to defend Xiuzhou. Commander Song moved his forces and encamped at Zuili Pavilion. There he held a banquet for the commanders, rewarded the troops, and discussed how to deploy the army and capture Hangzhou. Then Chai Jin, the Little Whirlwind, rose and said, “Ever since you saved my life at Gaotangzhou, elder brother, I have constantly enjoyed your affectionate care. I have sat here sharing honor and riches without ever repaying your kindness and fellowship. Now I wish to penetrate deep into Fang La’s lair and serve as a spy. Perhaps I may win some merit in battle, repay the court, and bring honor to you as well. I do not know whether you will permit it.” Song Jiang was delighted and said, “If you, my lord, are willing to enter the bandits’ lair itself and learn the twists and turns of its streams and mountains, we can advance our troops, capture the rebel chief Fang La alive, and send him under guard to the capital. Only then shall our small service be made manifest, and we shall share honor and riches together. I fear only that the journey will be too arduous for you to undertake.” Chai Jin said, “I am willing to risk death and make the journey. It would be best, however, if Yan Qing accompanied me. He understands the local speech of every region and can moreover act as circumstances require.” Song Jiang said, “I shall grant everything you have asked, worthy brother. But Yan Qing has been assigned to Commander Lu’s force, so we must send an official dispatch to summon him.” Before their discussion had ended, a messenger reported, “Commander Lu has specially sent Yan Qing to announce a victory.

p.src: Yan Qing entered the camp, went up to the command tent, and bowed to Song Jiang, after which he ate and drank. Song Jiang asked, “Did you come by water, worthy brother? Or did you come overland?” Yan Qing replied, “I came here by boat.” Song Jiang asked again, “When Dai Zong returned, he said that the troops had already advanced to attack Huzhou. How did matters turn out?” Yan Qing reported, “After leaving Xuanzhou, Commander Lu divided the army into two forces. The commander personally led one thousand troops against Huzhou, killed the false governor Gong Wen and five of his subordinate officers, subdued Huzhou, scattered the rebel troops, and pacified the people. He then sent an official report to Pacification Commissioner Zhang, assigned a control officer to defend the city, and specially ordered me to come and announce the victory. The half of the forces assigned by our commander was placed under Lin Chong and sent ahead to capture Dusong Pass, after which all are to rendezvous at Hangzhou. When I departed, I heard that fighting took place daily on the road to Dusong Pass, but the pass could not be taken, so the commander went there with Zhu Wu. He entrusted General Huyan with command of the troops guarding Huzhou. Once the central command sends a control officer to protect the region and pacify its people, that force will advance on Deqing County and then join us at Hangzhou.” Song Jiang asked again, “Tell me the names of the commanders and officers divided between the two places—those defending Huzhou and taking Deqing, and those transferred to fight at Dusong Pass. How many went to each, and how many remained with Huyan Zhuo?” Yan Qing said, “I have the list here.”

p.src: Meanwhile, Strategist Wu Yong spoke again to Song Jiang: “South of Hangzhou lies the great Qiantang River, which gives access to the islands of the sea. If several men could take a small boat along the coast, enter through Zheshan Gate, and set off signal cannon and raise signal flags on the riverbank outside the South Gate, the city would surely be thrown into panic. Which of your naval leaders shall make the attempt?” Before he had finished, Zhang Heng and the three Ruan brothers cried, “We shall all go!” Song Jiang said, “The western approach to Hangzhou also borders lakes and will likewise require naval forces. You cannot all go.” Wu Yong said, “We need send only Zhang Heng and Ruan Xiaoqi, with Hou Jian and Duan Jingzhu aboard.” They immediately assigned the four men, who took more than thirty sailors, a dozen or so signal cannon, and signal flags, went to the coast to find a boat, and set out for the Qiantang River.

p.src: Let us say no more of the two armies that had gone to provide support. Meanwhile, Vanguard Song's main army advanced steadily until it reached Mount Linping, where they saw a red banner waving atop the mountain. Song Jiang at once dispatched two of his commanders, Hua Rong and Qin Ming, to scout the road ahead, then ordered the warships and carts hurried across the Chang'an Dam. Hua Rong and Qin Ming led a thousand troops around the spur of the mountain and promptly encountered Shi Bao's southern army. Two foremost commanders under Shi Bao saw Hua Rong and Qin Ming and rode out together. One was Wang Ren and the other Feng Yi; each leveled a long spear and charged. From the Song ranks, Hua Rong and Qin Ming deployed their troops and rode out to meet them. Qin Ming brandished his wolf-fanged mace and made straight for Feng Yi; Hua Rong leveled his spear and engaged Wang Ren. The four horses crossed, and after more than ten bouts neither side had gained the advantage. When Qin Ming and Hua Rong saw that reinforcements stood behind the southern army, they both called out, “Let us pause!” Each wheeled his horse and returned to the formation. Hua Rong said, “We must not become entangled in battle. Hurry and report to our elder brother, so that we may devise another plan.” The rear ranks immediately sent a swift report to the central army. Song Jiang led the four commanders Zhu Tong, Xu Ning, Huang Xin, and Sun Li straight to the battlefront. Wang Ren and Feng Yi of the southern army rode out once more to fight, shouting abuse: “Defeated wretches, how dare you come out to do battle again!” Qin Ming flew into a rage, brandished his wolf-fanged mace, and spurred his horse forward to fight Feng Yi again. Wang Ren challenged Hua Rong to come out, but Xu Ning rode forward alone and charged with his spear leveled. Hua Rong and Xu Ning were a matched pair, the Silver Spearman and the Golden Spearman. Hua Rong at once spurred after Xu Ning, took bow and arrow in hand, and before Xu Ning and Wang Ren could cross weapons, watched until the range was close enough and loosed a single shaft. Wang Ren was shot from his horse, and the entire southern army turned pale. Seeing Wang Ren shot from his horse, Feng Yi was startled and caught unprepared. Qin Ming struck him squarely on the head with his mace and knocked him from the saddle, whereupon the southern troops scattered and fled. The Song forces charged after them. Unable to withstand the attack, Shi Bao withdrew to Mount Gaoting and made camp near Dongxin Bridge. By then evening had fallen, and since no firm plan could be established, the southern troops withdrew into the city for the time being.
